title: Edit Distance
statement: Return the minimum number of operations needed to turn `word1` into `word2`. One operation **inserts** a letter, **deletes** a letter or **replaces** a letter.

example.why: horse → rorse (replace h by r) → rose (delete r) → ros (delete e).

idea: Let `dp[i][j]` be the cheapest way to turn the first `i` letters of `word1` into the first `j` letters of `word2`.
If the two last letters are **equal**, nothing has to be done for them: `dp[i][j] = dp[i − 1][j − 1]`.
Otherwise pay 1 for the best of three moves: **replace** the letter (then solve `dp[i − 1][j − 1]`), **delete** it from word1 (`dp[i − 1][j]`), or **insert** word2's letter (`dp[i][j − 1]`).

complexity.timeWhy: One cell per pair of prefix lengths, each in O(1).
complexity.spaceWhy: The table (two rows would be enough).

steps.text: Our example: **`word1 = "horse", word2 = "ros"`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
First column: turning the first i letters of `word1` into the **empty** string takes i deletions.

views.title: dp[i][j] = operations to turn word1[:i] into word2[:j]

steps.text: First row: building the first j letters of `word2` from the **empty** string takes j insertions.
